state:
Goal `core-str-3-3` is reached: its one check, `dossier-core-str-3-3`, reports nothing owed and
0 failed over all twelve members. `wrap` was the last. It used to build a Rust `String` and a
table of one `usize` per character before its result, and the memory limit saw neither. `wrapped`
is now one pass that keeps byte offsets and a character count, and writes through `built`, which
asks the limit before each growth (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/str.rs` `wrapped`'s doc). Its card and
the `WRAP_OPTIONS` comment claimed PHP's default break is `" \n"`; PHP's is `"\n"`, and both now
say so. Every `Core\Str` perf record was re-measured after `str.rs` changed. `wrap` measures one
allocation per call.
